text: Grateful for Dr. Kittiwan. I needed to get back on my ADHD meds to improve my work performance. I called and was able to come in the same day! No long wait. Quick & straightforward service. Fair prices.

Great experience, super easy to get the medicine you need refilled, doctor is very friendly and kind. I suggest call ahead, she will answer any questions you have and you can usually just walk right in after

She only cares about taking your money, barely even acknowledged me during our consultation. She prescribed Alprazolam to me without mentioning that it is highly addictive and extremely dangerous when mixed with alcohol (I have a friend who died of this combination). Extremely irresponsible and a disgrace to the psychiatric community

I haven't used the clinic yet, but I've taken my son to the hospital for consultations. The doctor listened to my concerns.
He answered my questions and was very patient.

There are good and bad points, balancing out. But there's one thing I don't know if the doctor does this to other patients: when I'm sharing my story, if a foreign patient comes in or a phone call comes in, they usually choose to leave me and answer the call or walk out of the room to talk to the foreigner. Or sometimes they yawn while I'm telling my story or venting...

But I try to think, okay, maybe my case isn't that serious, or maybe my voice is too monotonous and soft, so the doctor is sleepy...

The doctor's office door is never closed, so when other patients come in for consultations or to share their stories, the people waiting can hear everything... It might be good in that the people listening might realize they're not alone in their problems, but on the other hand, I wonder if this should be a private matter... Once, I confided in the doctor about my suicidal thoughts. My desire to die was to escape the actions of my family. The sentence that still haunts me is, "You're just a chick in my hand; I can squeeze you to death or let you live." ... It left me numb, and they reinforced it by saying that my condition will never go away because of various external factors. If I'm weak, I'll have to take medication forever. It's important to point out that this is normal.

But... what's the point of seeing a doctor if we have to think like this...?

The doctor has his good points too. Initially, he understood and listened, but lately, I've started to feel like he's not paying much attention...

Or maybe it's because I'm still sick that these feelings arise and I need more attention to compensate for the lack of support at home. But honestly, from the first day I went to see the doctor, trying to meet, consult/vent, getting medication, until today, almost three years later, this month has been the most self-destructive...

I hope this review will be helpful to anyone considering becoming a client of this doctor...

This was a terrible experience with this doctor. It cost me 800 baht within 15 minutes, and he just rushed to give me the medicine without listening or explaining properly. It's no different from being a pharmacy doctor or psychiatrist. I definitely don't recommend him.

I waited a very long time. From the moment I arrived at the clinic until I saw the doctor and left, it took 40 minutes! The elderly doctor was very impolite.
They only care about money. The clinic only cares about money (I wanted to pay to come see them).
This is a terrible psychiatric clinic in Chiang Mai.

The doctor listened and gave good advice. The medicine cost was very good. I'd like to thank the doctor very much for providing treatment and listening to me all along. There's also a psychotherapist here. This is the only place where you can get everything you need. The doctor speaks English very well.
